messages.subject: Re: conditional sidebarPanel based on tab
messages.body_plain:
You need an 'id' as the last parameter for 'tabsetPanel':

tabsetPanel(
  tabPanel("Heatmap", textOutput("k"),plotOutput("heatmap",width = "1000px", height = "1000px"),value=1),
  tabPanel("About", textOutput("about"),textOutput("about_test"),value=2)

  , id = "thisisanid"
)

Hope that helps, L

messages.subject: Access input$... in ui.R
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am just discovering Shiny and loving it. So first off, thanks very much!

Now, I have created an app which reads a file with time series for a large number of variables, offers to select a few variables through checkboxGroupInput() and plots the corresponding time series (using ggplot + facet_grid).

So my `ui.R` looks basically like:

load("mydata.Rdata")
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  sidebarPanel(
    checkboxGroupInput("vars", "Vars", names(mydata))
  ),
  mainPanel(
    plotOutput("seriesPlot")
  )
))

Of course, since the height of plotOutput is fixed, the height of each series (each facet) becomes smaller when more variables are selected. I would like the height of the plot to grow with the number of variables selected. I don't need it to be very precise, so, for example, I would be very happy to have

    plotOutput("seriesPlot", height=length(input$vars) * 100)

to allocate ~100px per variable. But the `input` variable is unknown at this point.

How could I achieve this?
Thank you very much in advance!

Jean-Olivier Irisson

messages.subject: Re: Help me out of nested reactives
messages.subject_clean: Help me out of nested reactives
messages.body_plain:
The key is that if you use a reactive expression (formerly known as "reactive function"), its value gets cached, and it only re-executes when it depends on variables that have changed. So you could do something like this to use cleaned data in two output objects, and it'll only execute the clean_data() reactive expression once:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  clean_data <- reactive ({
    # Do something based on input$foo, and return a data frame
  })

  output$mytable <- renderTable({
    clean_data()
  })

  output$myplot <- renderPlot({
    data <- clean_data()
    plot(data$x, data$y)
  })
})

Note that this code is written for Shiny 0.4.0; if you want it to work with previous versions:
* Replace reactive({ }) with reactive(function() { })
* Replace renderTable({ }) with reactiveTable(function() { })
* Replace renderPlot({ }) with reactivePlot(function() { })

There are some new parts of the tutorial that explain how this works:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview

-Winston

Right now there's not a simply way to send arbitrary .png files to the browser. renderPlot() only works with code that can be wrapped in `png(); ... ; dev.off()`, and it will send the output to the client. There have been a few questions on the mailing list which could use this capability, though, so it's something we'll think about adding.

It's not possible to use input$ variables directly in ui.r, since the code in ui.r simply generates an HTML page. However, you can use the approach discussed here (you've probably read this already, but just in case...):

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/4E5rJlHlnZA/discussion

To make it work, you'll need to get the latest version of Shiny from github. Good luck!

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
Hey guys,
I am *very* new to all this but think I found a workable solution.  It all comes down to the bootstrap scaffolding.  I was trying to get 4 data inputs into one line and found this thread.  I think if you include an "offset" column then you will get the desired result.  This is from what I am working on:

    div(class='row',
        div(class="span2 offset1", numericInput("CPC", "CPC:", .392,min=0,max=1,step=0.001)),
        div(class="span2", numericInput("LPC", "LPC:", .189,min=0,max=1,step=0.001)),
        div(class="span2", numericInput("NDP", "NDP:", .306,min=0,max=1,step=0.001)),
        div(class="span2", numericInput("GRN", "GRN:", .061,min=0,max=1,step=0.001))
    ),
    tags$style(type="text/css", '#CPC {width: 50px;}'),
    tags$style(type="text/css", '#LPC {width: 50px;}'),
    tags$style(type="text/css", '#NDP {width: 50px;}'),
    tags$style(type="text/css", '#GRN {width: 50px;}'),

It worked for me.  Hope that helps!
Best,
John

cleaned_data <- reactive({
   input$foo
   source("blah.R") #uses input$foo dataset and outputs cleaned_data and another_cleaned_data
   return(cleaned_data)
   #how can I return another_cleaned_data as well?  Make a nested another_cleaned_data() reactive?  I'm sure that's not the answer.  And I want all the processing done in blah.R
})

On Monday, March 4, 2013 11:54:29 AM UTC-5, Winston Chang wrote:
> The key is that if you use a reactive expression (formerly known as "reactive function"), its value gets cached, and it only re-executes when it depends on variables that have changed. So you could do something like this to use cleaned data in two output objects, and it'll only execute the clean_data() reactive expression once:
>
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>   clean_data <- reactive ({
>     # Do something based on input$foo, and return a data frame
>   })
>
>   output$mytable <- renderTable({
>     clean_data()
>   })
>
>   output$myplot <- renderPlot({
>     data <- clean_data()
>     plot(data$x, data$y)
>   })
> })
>
>
> Note that this code is written for Shiny 0.4.0; if you want it to work with previous versions:
> * Replace reactive({ }) with reactive(function() { })
> * Replace renderTable({ }) with reactiveTable(function() { })
> * Replace renderPlot({ }) with reactivePlot(function() { })
>
>
> There are some new parts of the tutorial that explain how this works:
> http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview
>
>
> -Winston
>

> >

I end up with nested reactive functions because when I first started playing with shiny, it was the only way my app would work.  Now it's become a habit and I don't know how to get out of it.  I think I need to use observe() or functions, but I don't know how to use them here. Here's the gist of how my server.R usually looks:

On Monday, March 4, 2013 6:25:10 PM UTC+1, Winston Chang wrote:
> Hi Jean-Olivier -
>
> It's not possible to use input$ variables directly in ui.r, since the code in ui.r simply generates an HTML page. However, you can use the approach discussed here (you've probably read this already, but just in case...):

Thanks Winston. I did not read this topic no. I was searching for a more generic answer. But it is indeed exactly what I need and it works with the latest version of shiny. So thanks a lot.

Still, the more general problem is of interest to me since, for a different application, I have this use case:

the user selects various variables in a dataset (various species) and the same analysis is run for each of these species. For each analysis/species, I want to output a summary text and a few plots. So I would want to loop over input$species and call textOutput and several plotOutput for each of them successively.

The only way that I see to achieve this currently is to prepare n (10 or so) textOutput + plotOutput calls, let the user select m species (with m <= n) and fill the first m calls with something, while leaving the rest blank. Not very elegant or scalable. What could be a better solution?

Thanks in advance!

Jean-Olivier Irisson

messages.subject: Saving/loading shiny session state?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

we've been using shiny internally for (to use big words) "exploratory data analysis" in a project for some time and it's absolutely fabulous. However, working with a shiny application shows that there is a number of capabilities that "would be very nice to have". I understand that proper authentication (and maybe user management/authorization) will be introduced later - at least in the "enterprise edition". What I would be after now is saving and reloading session state.

Two use cases as example:
- The user works on the data (effectively clicks around for some time, changing inputs) and finds just the visualization he wants. He closes the browser; next time when he opens it, he would like to see this state.
- The user wants to be able to record visualization states (for various "findings") and recall them one-by-one for a live, step-by-step demonstration.

At some level, both cases boil down to the ability to save and load (full or partial) session states. I think that to some extent this can be done manually in the code (I haven't really had the time to think through and implement the tricks that seem to be applicable); my question is whether there is "platform support" or is it in the scope of future development at all.

Best regards
Imre

messages.subject: How could one post to a wordpress blog, like the googleVis package
messages.subject_clean: How could one post to a wordpress blog, like the googleVis package
messages.body_plain:
Great package, thanks for building. Is it possible to render interactive charts in self-hosted blog posts like one can with the googleVis + R package?

Using googleVis output with WordPress <https://code.google.com/p/google-motion-charts-with-r/wiki/UsingWordPress>

WordPress <http://wordpress.org/> is a popular web software for creating websites and blogs. Here we give some tips about the usage with googleVis output.

By default WordPress does not allow JavaScript code (and hence googleVis output) to be inserted into a page. However, additional plugins allow us to extend the functions of WordPress.

One option of embedding JavaScript code inside a WordPress post is to use the "custom fields shortcode" <http://wordpress.org/extend/plugins/custom-fields-shortcode> plugin. This plugin allows you to create a custom field for the googleVis code, which can be referred to in your article.

Suppose you created a motion chart in R:
M <- gvisMotionChart(Fruits, "Fruit", "Year",
                     options=list(width=400, height=370))

Copy the chart code, e.g. from
print(M, 'chart')

and paste it into the value text area of a custom field in WordPress, e.g. with instance name Fruits. To include the motion chart into your article add [cf]Fruits[/cf] into the post, see the figure below for an illustration. For more details see also the vignette <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/googleVis/vignettes/googleVis.pdf>.

messages.subject: Re: Performance, parallelism
messages.body_plain:
Shiny Server is not fundamentally serial but R is. Right now Shiny Server directs all users for a given app to the same R process, which is why all users end up being serial.

There are two ways to address this (that can be used in combination).

1) Run multiple Shiny Server processes and/or machines and put them behind a load balancer. For multiple Shiny Server processes per machine, you'd need to have a config file per Shiny Server process and have each process listening on a different port.
2) Configure Shiny Server to launch multiple processes for a given app. This isn't currently possible but is on the plan for later this year.

How urgent is the bottleneck for you right now? Is the app unusable for you as deployed right now, or was it just right after your announcement?

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Many of you have been waiting patiently for file upload improvements in Shiny, especially fixing file uploads on Shiny Server. We're pretty close now, but it involved writing a whole lot of new code so I'd like to see some beta testing before we release to CRAN.

Please help us beta test by following the upgrade instructions at the end of this message.

Features:
Now works with Shiny Server! (glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com> is already upgraded)
Local uploads are also much faster and more robust
Progress is displayed during upload
Limitations:
(Still) not compatible with IE9 and earlier
Uploads cannot be canceled (other than reloading the page)
Note:
By default, Shiny limits file upload requests to 5MB; anything larger will be rejected. You can change this limit using option(shiny.maxRequestSize = x), where x is the size in bytes; a size of -1 means any size is allowed.
----

Instructions for upgrading a Shiny Server install:

Run these commands from the shell:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))\""

sudo npm install -g https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/tarball/httpuv

Then restart Shiny Server. If you're using Upstart, the command is sudo restart shiny-server

Instructions for upgrading a non-server Shiny install:

Run this command from the R console:

install.packages('shiny', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))

Then restart your R session.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server and systemd
messages.body_plain:
Ok, I took a stab at making a systemd compatible script.
I put the following (in between the dashed lines below) into a file (shiny.service) and copied that file to /lib/systemd/system.  This is on Fedora 16.  Then I ran the following commands as sudo.

1) sudo systemctl daemon-reload
2) sudo systemctl start shiny.service

Then I went to an app and sure enough, it works.

I think you can add the following line to end of the [Service] unit to
tell systemd to automatically restart this service when it dies.
Restart=restart-always

---------shiny.service------------------------
[Unit]
Description=shiny-server deploys R shiny applications
After=syslog.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/shiny-server
Type=forking

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
---------------------------------------

Since it's my first post on this group I would like to start with saying "Hi" to everybody and "Thank you" the dev team for great work on Shiny.

I have similar problem with application I'm developing and running on Shiny Server.
In the first attempt I used the cluster module from Node.js as shown here: http://nodejs.org/api/cluster.html

I modified the https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/lib/main.js file in the following way:

//[modules, variables, etc.]
if (cluster.isMaster) {
  for (var i = 0; i < numCPUs; i++) {
    cluster.fork();
  }
  cluster.on('exit', function(worker, code, signal) {
    console.log('worker ' + worker.process.pid + ' died');
  });
} else {
   //[original main.js code]
}
The server started correctly, node process was spawned 4 times (4 cores VM); while trying to access the apps the R processes started (one R process per each node process), but no response was send to the browser. It seems to me that there is some problem with sockjs not being able to talk to browser from node.js child process. Maybe you can help with that.

Now I am trying to achieve the parallelization from within R - I am using the multicore::parallel function to fork most computationally expensive functions to other process(es) and periodically run multicore::collect from main process to determine if computation is done. So far looks simple and promising, I'll share the results when I finish the implementation.

messages.subject: Re: Performance, parallelism
messages.body_plain:
Hmm, the problem I currently have is actually that our local NIS server cluster is poorly performing.

It seems that unlike most server applications, R makes a lot of calls onto NIS, via getpwuid.

This function is called by do_fileinfo  - presumably invoked by file.info <http://file.info>.

For some reason, file.info <http://file.info> always retrieves (via an internal function) the uid translated into the username - even if it has asked the same question MANY times before.

part of this problem is that I'm using a network user, but my company policies make this (if not unavoidable) very hard to avoid.

As you guys are R core - can you suggest any way to cause caching of UID->username lookup?

I'm considering building an LD_PRELOAD'ed cache.

-Alex

> > Shiny Server is not fundamentally serial but R is. Right now Shiny Server directs all users for a given app to the same R process, which is why all users end up being serial.
> >
> > There are two ways to address this (that can be used in combination).
> >
> > 1) Run multiple Shiny Server processes and/or machines and put them behind a load balancer. For multiple Shiny Server processes per machine, you'd need to have a config file per Shiny Server process and have each process listening on a different port.
> > 2) Configure Shiny Server to launch multiple processes for a given app. This isn't currently possible but is on the plan for later this year.
> >
> > How urgent is the bottleneck for you right now? Is the app unusable for you as deployed right now, or was it just right after your announcement?
> >
> >
> > On Tue, Mar 5, 2013 at 12:15 PM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:

okay, I've completely hacked pwuid and gui lookups out of the loop and it's a lot faster.

Makefile
#
# Makefile
#

all: libs

#
# Make a shared Library
#
libs: getpwuid.c
        gcc -shared -Wl,-soname,libfuncs.so.1 -o libfuncs.so.1.0  getpwuid.c
        ln -s libfuncs.so.1.0 libfuncs.so.1
        ln -s libfuncs.so.1 libfuncs.so

getpwuid.c
/*
 Put all the functions you want to override here
*/
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <pwd.h>

struct passwd *getpwuid(uid_t uid)
{
    return 0;
}

struct group *getgrgid(gid_t gid)
{
    return 0;
}

build and use:
make
setenv LD_PRELOAD $PWD/libfuncs.so.1.0

messages.subject: Re: Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Reactive refers to the API - it doesn't rely on you constructing function calls and registering callbacks - graphs and tables that need updating when you change inputs just change automatically.

It does have javascript in it to implement this feature, but you don't need to worry about javascript unless you extend it.  You don't need to write any javascript at all.

You describe (on the server, in R) or in HTML, a web page containing inputs and outputs such as images (plots), text (html) and tables (html).

You also describe (in the form of R functions on the server) how outputs are connected to inputs:

Here's a very simple example of a server function:

output$renderPlot({ plot(1:input$maxVal) })

-Alex

Have done, I have cc'ed Joe on my submission.

Extra diagnosis:

library() calls file.info <http://file.info> to check if a library is a directory.

file.info <http://file.info> calls getpwuid.

really it should call file_test, and in turn, file_test should use a (non existent) do_isdir function in platform.c which uses stat, not do_fileinfo.

-Alex

messages.subject: Multiple shiny apps, issue with rendering subpages
messages.subject_clean: Multiple shiny apps, issue with rendering subpages
messages.body_plain:
Hey guys,

I am new to Shiny, and I am totally impressed with it.

I played a bit with it, but I found a small issue I am unable to solve (I am novice to programming in general).

I want to have several small shiny apps running on different ports, and I want to combine them on a webpage with bootstrap template and couple of pages that will link apps via <iframe>. However, I am obviously missing some key elements.

Here is my ui.R:

library(shiny)
shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  includeHTML('../html/www/index.html')
))
index.html is just Bootstrap template with <iframe> pointing to localhost and different port for application.

messages.subject: Re: Computing a variable once
messages.body_plain:
Saptarshi -

It should only run messages() once when an input value changes. You can check this by inserting a print() statement in messages() and seeing how many times it prints out the value. I know it looks like it will be run twice, but Shiny does work to make sure it's only run once. It caches the value and simply hands it out, until an input value changes.

This page (and the next two) in the tutorial explains it in more depth:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity-overview

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Performance, parallelism
messages.body_plain:
The multicore::parallel seems to be working nice with Shiny, with additional advantage of giving live feedback from worker process.
A simple example of implementation:

1) Simulate expensive function:

f <- function(x) {
for(i in 1:3) {
multicore::sendMaster(as.character(i))
Sys.sleep(2)
}
sqrt(x)
}
2) Run in server:

values <- reactiveValues( res=NULL, calcMsg1 = NULL )
observe( {
if (is.null(proc)) {
proc <<- multicore::parallel(f( 10 )))
values$calcMsg1 <- 'Started'
invalidateLater(1000)
} else if ( multicore::selectChildren(proc) == multicore::processID(proc) ) {
res <- multicore::collect(proc, wait=FALSE)[[1]]
if( class(res) == 'character' ) {
invalidateLater(1000)
values$calcMsg1 <- res
} else {
multicore::collect(proc)
proc <<- NULL
values$res <- res
values$calcMsg1 <-  paste('FINISHED:',res)
}
} else { invalidateLater(1000); }
}, label='CalcMain', suspended = FALSE )

After execution we have final result in values$res.
While execution we can send feedback to browser using values$calcMsg1.

Notes:

proc = NULL was initially defied inside shinyServer function parameters, e.g. shinyServer(function(input, output, proc = NULL) { ...
This allows different browser connections fork multiple workers, while only 1 worker is allowed per connection. I believe it can be also defined as reactive value.

Last multicore::collect(proc) is mainly to ensure that R cleaned-up after forking and we would not run into memory problems.

I advise to use multicore::children() to limit number of workers depending on number of cores and available memory.

The function assumes that message class is 'character' and final result class is NOT 'character'. This can be easily fixed by defining and returning e.g. "message" class object.

Joe, you are right that this would not work for all apps, but in case of app with one/few expensive function(s) (e.g. calculating on big datasets) and many light functions (e.g plotting) it seems to work OK.
.

messages.subject: Re: Can someone please explain to me what "Passing functions to 'reactive' is deprecated." means
messages.subject_clean: Can someone please explain to me what "Passing functions to 'reactive' is deprecated." means
messages.body_plain:
You used to do this:

foo <- reactive(function() {
  data <- read.csv('foo.csv')
  subset(data, !is.na <http://is.na>(data$total))
})

With 0.4.0, you remove the "function()" part of it. The below is exactly equivalent to the above, only without the deprecation warning:

foo <- reactive({
  data <- read.csv('foo.csv')
  subset(data, !is.na <http://is.na>(data$total))
})

messages.subject: request: renderHTML
messages.body_plain:
renderUI creates a div.  It also creates the expectation that new interactive UI elements are created.

renderText will only expect text input.  A tags$h4 will cause an error.

renderPrint converts tags$h4 into quoted HTML.

What if...

I want to output a h4?

I want to output a span

I want to output a span with interactive elements in?

Please create:

1) renderHTML analog to renderText that renders the html generated by the expression, without the expectation that it generates UI.

Note - you could use the same mechanism that you use for reactives to _detect_ UI in renderText and renderHTML, and re-register inputs accordingly.

2) the option to build renderUI with span (or anything).

-Alex

I am trying to create a multipage Shiny web application. I would like to split functionality across several "server.R" files, which have specific html UI templates, but share the data objects.

 Am I right that Shiny can process only a single "index.html" file in "www" folder? Does it mean that I have to create a separate Shiny app for each individual task in separate folder? What about sharing data across several server.R files then?

Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: request: renderHTML
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

Great questions as usual.

renderUI itself actually does not create a div, it's the uiOutput/htmlOutput that creates it. You can replace uiOutput/htmlOutput with something like these examples:

tags$h4(id='foo', class='shiny-html-output')
tags$span(id='bar', class='shiny-html-output')

It would be great though to add a "tag" parameter to uiOutput and htmlOutput so you don't need to know this secret incantation.

Also, the framework has no special expectation that renderUI generates UI. It's uiOutput/htmlOutput (and the class="shiny-html-output" that they both generate) that tells Shiny that there might be UI. There's no harm at all in not having UI in these outputs though.

Hope that helps.

-joe

messages.subject: Re: HTML-based UI in multiple files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anton,

Each R process can only run a single Shiny app. Each Shiny app is only designed to run a single page. (Although some people e.g. Vincent Nijs have experimented with multiple HTML files with a single server.R)

One solution is to try to redesign your app to be a single page that switches through different "modes" (you could use tabsetPanel or get fancier with JavaScript, and some other people here like Vincent have implemented navbars).

We might be able to provide more feedback if you could disclose a little of what these different pages will do and how they relate to each other.

-joe

messages.subject: Re: Help me out of nested reactives
messages.subject_clean: Help me out of nested reactives
messages.body_plain:
Are you sure we didn't recommend you use reactiveValue and observers to implement insulated reactives? I couldn't find the thread where we talked about this so for the benefit of everyone let me expound on laziness and insulation.

We use the term "laziness" to mean: when a reactive expression (what we used to call reactive functions, before Shiny 0.4.0) notices that one of the reactive values/expressions that it depends on has changed, it does nothing other than notifying its dependent reactive expressions/observers that it has been invalidated. It doesn't re-execute itself or schedule itself to be re-executed.

We use the term "insulation" to mean that if one of the reactive values/expressions in your graph of dependencies (things that YOU depend on, not the other way around) changes, but before the chain reaches you the value is noticed to be the same as it was before, then you don't get invalidated. Here's a concrete example.

approxCount <- reactive({
  input$count - (input$count %% 10)
})

observe({
  cat(paste("Count has reached:", approxCount()))
})

The approxCount reactive expression rounds input$count to the nearest 10. So if input$count changes from 1 to 2, approxCount's value is recalculated and the result is 0 in both cases.

If reactive expressions don't provide insulation, then as input$count goes from 0, 1, 2... 10 you will see the output printed 11 times, with many duplicates. If reactive expressions provide insulation, then you will only see the output printed twice, with no duplicates.

Before Shiny 0.4.0, reactive functions were not lazy but provided insulation.
With Shiny 0.4.0, reactive expressions (née functions) are lazy but do not provide insulation.

It is not possible to have a single reactive construct that provides both laziness and insulation--these two goals are inherently exclusive. In real-world apps it appeared to us that laziness mattered way more often than insulation did. (For example, if you want tabs that are not showing to not cost you any recalculation time, you need laziness.)

It would be possible to introduce a different construct (insulatingReactive(), or maybe reactive({..}, lazy=FALSE)) that provides insulation, but we don't have one today. However you can combine reactiveValue and observers to achieve insulation:

values <- reactiveValues(approxCount=NULL)

observe({
  values$approxCount <- input$count - (input$count %% 10)
})

observe({
  cat(paste("Count has reached:", values$approxCount))
})

I'm not sure how you would combine reactiveValue and observers to achieve laziness though, or why you'd need to do anything special to get laziness in Shiny 0.4.0.

library(shiny)

Hi Joe -

This is awesome. I'm trying to write a little app that allows users to upload and process some CSVs of temperature traces. The app's on glimmer (http://glimmer.rstudio.com/ajayp/SUMS/).

I'm noticing some very bizarre behavior -- the loaded csvs repeat the first ~81 lines twice and then print the whole file. I've attached here a sample csv and will paste some code in below for my file upload. When I upload the same csv to a directory on the server and access it through list.files, i don't run into any problems. Any thoughts, if time permits, would be greatly appreciated.

Ajay

server.r

  # Return the requested dataset
  datasetInput <- reactive({
if(input$dataset=="Upload a File"){
   inFile <- input$file1
   if (is.null(inFile))
     return(NULL)
   dataset<-read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=T, stringsAsFactors =F)
   #write.csv(dataset,file=paste("/home/ajayp/data/",inFile[1],sep=""))
}
else{
   filepath<-paste('/home/ajayp/data/',input$dataset,sep="")
    dataset<-read.csv(filepath,header=T,stringsAsFactor=F)
    }
  })

ui.r

  sidebarPanel(
   #select a dataset - doesn't dynamically reload? why??
    selectInput("dataset", "Choose a SUMS File:",
     choices = factor(c(list.files('/home/ajayp/data', pattern=".csv"),'Upload a File'))),
    conditionalPanel(
     condition = "input.dataset == 'Upload a File'",
     fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File',
             accept=c('text/csv')
            )
    ),
...
)

messages.subject: Early Implementation of a TreeGrid widget
messages.subject_clean: Early Implementation of a TreeGrid widget
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I would like to share this early implementation of a TreeGrid widget, which provides a way to display hierarchical data.

You can try it out with:
library(shiny)
runGitHub(repo='Shiny-sandbox','cafe876', ref="master", subdir="shiny-treegrid")

The widget comes from the jQuery EasyUI library <http://www.jeasyui.com/demo/main/index.php?plugin=TreeGrid&theme=default&dir=ltr&pitem=>, which has a many additional features that I didn't implement yet, like drag-and-drop, on-the-fly edition, and checkboxes.

I believe that this kind of widget has an important place in an analytic process, both to analyze and to edit data structures.

Currently, the most painful for me is the data input format.
Have a look at the transformation that was needed for the demo dataset...it is horrible.
In the end it is just a list of lists that will be converted to JSON, but I'm not used to these manipulations.
Therefore: any suggestions welcome !

Best,
NH

El viernes, 9 de noviembre de 2012 03:48:08 UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] escribió:
>
> > Is there a plan to add validation for user input fields client side i.e. a input field should be a number or string, etc
> Sure, that seems like a really good candidate for our next release.
> > How are server side errors propagated to the user/UI - for example, if you user requests invalid date range or the data doesn't exist, how would you display that information gracefully to the UI
> The easiest way right now is to simply use R's default error handling, e.g. stop("Invalid date range"). When these errors make it all the way to an output without being caught, they are displayed in place of the output. The default style is for the error to appear in red, prepended with the word "Error:" in bold, but that is all customizable using CSS.
> > Are there plans to add authentication support i.e. users, groups, permissions per view, etc (something similar to the django admin module which comes for free out of the box)
> Definitely user authentication. I don't know what granularity at which the permissions will apply. If you could describe the scenario you have in mind for django-like permissions, it would be hugely helpful. (You're welcome to e-mail me off-list if you don't want to publicize details of your app.)
> > Would there be support for automatically updating the UI without any user input e.g. push updates to the data to the user.
> Yes, we have not written up examples of this yet but the pieces are there.
>
> The most common way that changes ripple through the system is through users touching inputs, but another way that we already support is time-based invalidation. Here's an example I just wrote that has two different components that are varying over time:
>
> Demo: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/time/
> Source: https://gist.github.com/4044364
>
> This might not be intuitive yet if you're still getting your head around reactive programming, but the point is that the "invalidateLater" function is all that is needed to build, say, a reactiveFileInput function that pushes changed values through the system. An intrepid Shiny user could build such a function now, but if you wait until the next release we can probably save you the trouble.
> > Are there any limitations in using existing R packages like ggplot2/googleVis/ or tikz images
> No problem with ggplot2, and in general visualizations that write to R's default graphics device should work fine. googleVis will need some customization to work with Shiny, similar to the kind of stuff Markus had to do to get googleVis to work with R Markdown. I'm not familiar with tikz.
> > How would you stitch together more complicated applications - for example, if you expand on your stocks example and add another view which shows fundamental time-series data, how would the navigation work.
> Currently Shiny is focused on single-page apps, so you'd need to integrate all the views into a single page. Tabs actually work pretty nicely for that in a lot of cases: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mosaic/CIgeometry/
> > How would you add static data to pages
> Can you be more specific about "static data"?
> > What other widgets are you guys planning on adding
> We don't have anything specific planned right now, we're just waiting to see what people request.
>
> I'll add that we are more excited about helping folks in the community to design and package their own widgets that can be easily used by all Shiny users.
>
> Thanks for the great questions--hope that helps!
>

messages.subject: Re: dynamically set height in renderPlot?
messages.body_plain:
So I'm having an issue with the height settings. I initially pushed a Shiny app months ago and struggled to add dynamic plot heights, but was successful thanks to Joe -  height=function(){input$foo * 26}

I'm presenting the app tomorrow in an R meetup and now the height is an issue again -  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/awegro/RunningChase/

Here is my server.R code

  heightSize = function() {
    a = 60+as.integer(12*nrow(subset(x,Company == paste(input$company) & Gender != paste(input$variable,''))))
    if (a > 4000) '4000px' else a
  }

  # Generate a plot of the runners for the requested company by gender
  output$Runners <- reactivePlot(function() {
    p <- qplot(TotalTime/60,Name, data = subset(x,Company == paste(input$company) & Gender != paste(input$variable,'')), color = Gender)+xlab("Minutes")+ylab("Runner")+ ggtitle(paste(input$company))
    print(p)
  }, height = heightSize)

  output$Height <- reactiveText(heightSize)

I'm printing the output$Height value above the tabs and it's getting the right values, but the plot height isn't changing dynamically. I've been messing with the height settings for a couple hours trying to work around it adding height = 'auto' , as suggested by this post, to the ui.R file, but that gives me a blank plot.

Any suggestions? I'm guessing there have been a lot of upgrades to Shiny since I started using 0.2.4. The rstudio server version is 0.4.0.99

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server, Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server on Linux, and RODBC problem
messages.body_plain:
Anyone used the Microsoft ODBC driver to query SQL Server from RODBC and Shiny Server on Ubuntu?

We have installed Shiny Server on Ubuntu 12.04 (64 bit vm) with MS ODBC Driver 11 for SQL Server on Linux (http://msdn.microsoft.com/library/hh568451(SQL.110).aspx). Testing the driver installation with sqllcmd works fine. We are able to open a connection to the SQL server, select a database, and execute a query. We are also able to run a simple shiny app that queries the database we are trying to connect to. This simple app is running within R studio on a windows machine. However the same app on the Linux Shiney Server returns the following error:

Warning in odbcDriverConnect(paste0(driveStr, serverStr, database, authStr)) :
  [RODBC] ERROR: state IM002, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Data source name not found, and no default driver specified

The simple app was written using a connection string rather than DSN. The various parts of the connection string are idential to the string used on the windows app except the driver. On the Linux machine, we are using [SQL Server Native Client 11.0] as the driver, based on the response to odbcinst -q -d.

Thanks for any help.

messages.subject: Re: How to save data from user input for later use?
messages.subject_clean: How to save data from user input for later use?
messages.body_plain:
To keep a running list of the values the user has inputted, declare a variable at a per-session <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#scoping> level, and simply add new values to it as the user gives more inputs. Whenever you add to it, you could also write.csv the data to a local file--just make sure to generate a unique file name when the session begins, i.e.:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  logfile <- paste(
    './userlogs/',
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S"),
    round(runif(1, min=10000, max=99999)),
    '.csv',
    sep='')
  values <- data.frame(x=numeric(0), y=numeric(0))

  observe({
    # Assuming your saveButton is an actionButton, from the shiny-incubator <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator> package
    if (input$saveButton == 0)
      return()
    isolate({
      values <- rbind(values, c(x=input$x, y=input$y))
      write.csv(values, logfile)
    })
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: How to save data from user input for later use?
messages.subject_clean: How to save data from user input for later use?
messages.body_plain:
Is it likely Shiny will have a feature where you can (1) save the input-object directly to a file and (2) load it back-in with a button click? The next time you use your shiny app, input you could replaced it with the previous state.

On Monday, March 11, 2013 3:32:32 PM UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> To keep a running list of the values the user has inputted, declare a variable at a per-session <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#scoping> level, and simply add new values to it as the user gives more inputs. Whenever you add to it, you could also write.csv the data to a local file--just make sure to generate a unique file name when the session begins, i.e.:
>
> shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>   logfile <- paste(
>     './userlogs/',
>     format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S"),
>     round(runif(1, min=10000, max=99999)),
>     '.csv',
>     sep='')
>   values <- data.frame(x=numeric(0), y=numeric(0))
>
>   observe({
>     # Assuming your saveButton is an actionButton, from the shiny-incubator <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-incubator> package
>     if (input$saveButton == 0)
>       return()
>     isolate({
>       values <- rbind(values, c(x=input$x, y=input$y))
>       write.csv(values, logfile)
>     })
>   })
> })
>
>
> On Mon, Mar 11, 2013 at 11:08 AM, Matthew Holden <matthe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > I am writing an app that will asks the user to submit a numeric value via a slidebar, will then click a push button to continue, a plot is generated with that numeric value, call it y1, as a pont (1, y1) in an x,y plot. the app will then ask the user to do it again, he enters a new value, y2, and the new plot is of (1, y1) and (2, y2).
> >

I also am having problems with the re-plotting after each time step. I've looked over all the tutorial material, but am still confused on these issues.

  Error in data.frame(name = file$name, size = file$size, type = file$type,  :

messages.subject: Force output to reactivate
messages.body_plain:
I have sort of a weird application in which the output depends on the input but is non-deterministic. I would like the user to be able to re-generate the output with a submit button. I've implement this for the most part, except this doesn't work when the input doesn't change (since my output is a reactiveTable and thus won't re-run unless the input changes).

Is there a way to force re-generation of output based on button click without input changing? I would also settle with clearing the input to force the user to enter new input.

My code isn't worth posting... just a ui.R with a textInput and a server.R with a renderTable().

messages.subject: Re: Force output to reactivate
messages.body_plain:
You can use an actionButton, similar to this example:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/actionbutton/
  https://gist.github.com/wch/4963887

It sounds like you'll want to do one thing differently, though. In this example, the isolate() function is used so that it _only_ updates when button is clicked, but I think you don't want to use it in your case. (Assuming you want it to update if the input value is changed OR the button is clicked.)

More information on the code is here, as well as an explanation of isolate():
  http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#isolation

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: ggplot problem . "Error unused argument(s) (n)"
messages.body_plain:
It looks like you have plyr installed in your personal library but not ggplot2. ggplot2 is being taken from the site library (/usr/local/lib/R/site-library) where a version is being loaded that is not compatible with plyr 1.8.

You should either install ggplot2 in your personal library, or remove plyr from your personal library--either should fix it.

messages.subject: Updating a Shiny app?
messages.body_plain:
As a first foray into learning Shiny, I recently posted an app on glimmer and noticed some odd behaviour (maybe it isn't odd, and is just due to a lack of understanding on my part).  The app (a character and "bad guy" randomizer for a board game, Arkham Horror) was originally hosted at: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/msigal/arkhamrandomizer/ and it works as expected.

Based upon some feedback, I wanted to update the application to incorporate more investigators and such.  I did so and it worked locally, so I uploaded it to /arkhamrandomizer/... and I got a series of errors (about how my new input variables were unused).  However, if I upload it to a *different* directory, it works fine! (see http://glimmer.rstudio.com/msigal/arkhamrandv2/).

Is this because I didn't stop the Shiny server from v1 before replacing it with v2?  If so, how would I do that?

Sorry if this is a really elementary question!  I can't wait to implement more applications with Shiny!

messages.subject: Re: messages between client and server
messages.body_plain:
Capturing the inputs are easy. You could add this code to server.R, inside your server function:

observe({
  inputs <- as.list(input)
  # One example of saving, probably you'd want something more sophisticated:
  write.csv(inputs, "userinputs.csv", append=TRUE)
})

This would call write.csv with all the inputs whenever any one of them changed.

Saving the plot is harder. By far the cleanest route would be to take the inputs and re-generate the plots when you need them--if you factor your code into functions in a separate .R file, then this should be straightforward.

> However, I choosed Java, because these states should be saved to a graph, witch shows step-by-step, how the final form gained shape, preferably into an Xmind workbook ( http://www.xmind.net/ ), and it has a nice Java API, with I could make the needed workbook.

messages.subject_clean: How to save data from user input for later use?
messages.body_plain:
Yeah, it's on our list. We are getting close to the point where you'd be able to hack it in yourself (need access to the URL and the ability to set values on inputs) but we also would like to have this as a first-class feature.

messages.subject: Re: mapping URLs with shiny.
messages.body_plain:
Sort of. Each Shiny application is a single page and thus a single URL--there's nothing to map. (If you have assets like CSS, JavaScript, and images, those can be served up as separate URLs, but they are generally just mapped to a directory.)

Shiny Server <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server> is used to host one or more Shiny applications on a server, with each application getting a different URL; in that case you use a config file <http://htmlpreview.github.com/?https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/blob/master/config.html> to control the URL mapping.

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  myplot <- function() {
    #par(mfrow=c(3,1))
    mat <- matrix(c(1,2,3), 3, 1, byrow = TRUE)
    nf <- layout(mat, widths = c(200, 200, 200), height = c(100,100,100 ), TRUE)
    layout.show(nf)

    y1 <- rnorm(50)
      plot(y1)
    y2 <- rnorm(100)
      plot(y2)

    y3 <- rnorm(200)
      plot(y3)

  }

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({ myplot() })

  output$downloadData <- downloadHandler(
    filename = 'myplots.png',
    content = function(file) {
      png(file, width = 1000, height = 1000, units = "px", pointsize = 12, bg = "white", res = NA)
      myplot()

      dev.off()
    },
    contentType = 'image/png'
  )
})

I found my answer in the documentation <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/shiny.pdf>:

id: If provided, you can use input$id in your server logic to determine which of
the current tabs is active. The value will correspond to the value argument that
is passed to tabPanel.

Thank you!

messages.subject: Suggest: Reactive IO
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

  I have already started discussing this, but I would like to be able to place 'reactive IO' in UI.R.

  For example: inputOutputTextField("myname")

  They would not typically have a default value specified in UI.R

  In server.R there would be:

  input
  output
  variable

  Where variables behave like reactiveValues - they can be written from and read to.

  Writing to a variable$myname would update the text in the UI.

  It would also make the updated value available to all consumers of variable$myname, which would be automatically invoked as per the reactive mechanism.

  There might be a concept of an initial value function

  variableInit$myname = variableText({
    system.today()
  })

Use case 1:

  UI.R wants to contain a date field, which should have the value 'today', or the most recent ticket number.

  Since UI.R is fixed it may be hard to do this, or the data for the current user might not be available.

  server.R variable functions could do this easily.

Use Case 2:

  An input variable may have a number of valid values which is smaller than the set of values the user could input.  If the user inputs an invalid value, the value in the client should change to the nearest value value.

  server.R would take the value and (e.g.) round it, which would update the UI.  Note that race conditions between the user typing and the server updating may need to be dealt with.

Use Case 3:

  A change to a different input may be able to supply a new default value to the first input.

Alternative 1:

  reactiveUI or renderUI can be used to do this, but they are heavyweight and it slows down application start up.

  also the input values generated by inputs embedded in renderUI must pass from the server to the client and back before the server can take any action based upon them.  This has the effect of the application waking up panel by panel, which isn't as smart looking as I'd like.

  reactiveUI created inputs are created afresh each time the reactiveUI updates, which may create problems for e.g. javascript capturing events from those inputs.

Alternative 2:

  Javascript magic with hidden output fields being able to update input fields..

  This is how I currently handle it, but it hardly fits with the ease of use of the rest of shiny.  It also has some unpleasant possibilities for race conditions.

-Alex

messages.subject: Re: Suggest: Reactive IO
messages.body_plain:
These are excellent ideas which Winston and I have begun discussing as well. We want to make sure we design it carefully because as you point out there is the potential for race conditions and other edge cases that we want to make sure we at least know about.

If we get it "right" though, there's a chance the current notions of "input" and "output" won't be necessary anymore (though we would obviously want to provide backwards compatibility for today's Shiny apps). An input could just be a variable that happens never to be set from the server (other than the initial value), and an output could be a variable that the client never changes.

I am very excited by this line of thinking but we'll definitely be proceeding at a deliberate pace. In the meantime if you continue experimenting with Shiny we're happy to keep learning from your experiences!

On Fri, Mar 15, 2013 at 1:54 PM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
>   I have already started discussing this, but I would like to be able to place 'reactive IO' in UI.R.
>
>   For example: inputOutputTextField("myname")
>
>   They would not typically have a default value specified in UI.R
>
>   In server.R there would be:
>
>   input
>   output
>   variable
>
>   Where variables behave like reactiveValues - they can be written from and read to.
>
>   Writing to a variable$myname would update the text in the UI.
>
>   It would also make the updated value available to all consumers of variable$myname, which would be automatically invoked as per the reactive mechanism.
>
>   There might be a concept of an initial value function
>
>   variableInit$myname = variableText({
>     system.today()
>   })
>
> Use case 1:
>
>   UI.R wants to contain a date field, which should have the value 'today', or the most recent ticket number.
>
>   Since UI.R is fixed it may be hard to do this, or the data for the current user might not be available.
>
>   server.R variable functions could do this easily.
>
> Use Case 2:
>
>   An input variable may have a number of valid values which is smaller than the set of values the user could input.  If the user inputs an invalid value, the value in the client should change to the nearest value value.
>
>   server.R would take the value and (e.g.) round it, which would update the UI.  Note that race conditions between the user typing and the server updating may need to be dealt with.
>
> Use Case 3:
>
>   A change to a different input may be able to supply a new default value to the first input.
>
> Alternative 1:
>
>   reactiveUI or renderUI can be used to do this, but they are heavyweight and it slows down application start up.
>
>   also the input values generated by inputs embedded in renderUI must pass from the server to the client and back before the server can take any action based upon them.  This has the effect of the application waking up panel by panel, which isn't as smart looking as I'd like.
>
>   reactiveUI created inputs are created afresh each time the reactiveUI updates, which may create problems for e.g. javascript capturing events from those inputs.
>
> Alternative 2:
>
>   Javascript magic with hidden output fields being able to update input fields..
>
>   This is how I currently handle it, but it hardly fits with the ease of use of the rest of shiny.  It also has some unpleasant possibilities for race conditions.

>
> -Alex

messages.subject: Nested uiOutput error: input => uiOutput => uiOutput => output
messages.subject_clean: Nested uiOutput error: input => uiOutput => uiOutput => output
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have a problem for design a nested input/output app.
My app can be simplified as the following steps:
0. Input dataset by textarea. i.e.: input$textarea.in <http://textarea.in>
1. Load dataset and show the name list of the imported dataset. User could select data by selectInput.  i.e: uiOutput("choosedata")
2. Compute the range of selected data and then display a sliderInput. i.e.: uiOutput("range")
3. Finally, compute the square of value selected by sliderInput. i.e.:verbatimTextOutput("range.out")

That is:
input$textare.in <http://textare.in> => output$choosedata => input$dataset => output$range => input$range.in <http://range.in> => output$range.out
                   |________uiOutput/renderUI________|     |_____uiOutput/renderUI_____|      (error here!)

The error will happen at step 3 after changing imported dataset.
To be more specific, the initial input format is:
Data.A 1 2 3 4 5
Data.B 6 7 8 9 10 11

Another input format is:
Data.C 1 3 5 7
Data.D 2 4 6 8

Steps 1 and 2 would automatically change, but step wont.
How to fix it?
Best

Note that the online app and code are following:

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/tchsieh/myapp/

#=========================
#ui.R
#=========================
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Title"),
  sidebarPanel(
    p("Text Area:"),
    tags$textarea(id="textarea.in <http://textarea.in>", rows=3, "Data.A 1 2 3 4 5 \nData.B 6 7 8 9 10 11"),
    uiOutput("choosedata"),
    uiOutput("range")
  ),

  mainPanel(
    h2("Test"),

    h3("Raw Data (step1: work!)"),
    verbatimTextOutput("textarea.out"),

    h3("Range of the selected data (step2: work!)"),
    verbatimTextOutput("summary"),

    h3("Squared of the selected value (step3:error when change Text area)"),
    verbatimTextOutput("range.out")

  )
))

#=========================
#server.R
#=========================
library(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  loadPaste <- reactive({
    text <- input$textarea.in <http://textarea.in>
    temp <- lapply(readLines(textConnection(text)), function(x) scan(text = x, what='char'))
    out <- list()
    out.name <http://out.name> <- 0
    for(i in seq_along(temp)){
      out.name <http://out.name>[i] <- temp[[i]][1]
      out[[i]] <- as.numeric(temp[[i]][-1])
    }
    names(out) <- t(data.frame(out.name <http://out.name>))
    out
  })

  output$textarea.out <- renderPrint({
    loadPaste()
  })

  output$choosedata <- renderUI({
    dataname <- names(loadPaste())
    dataList <- list()
    for(i in seq_along(dataname)){
      dataList[[i]] <- dataname[i]
    }
    selectInput("dataset", "Select dataset:", choices  = dataList, selected = dataList[1])
  })

  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    out <- loadPaste()
    id <- which(names(out) == input$dataset)
    mydata <- out[[id]]
    range(mydata)

  })

  output$range <- renderUI({
    out <- loadPaste()
    id <- which(names(out) == input$dataset)
    mydata <- out[[id]]
    sliderInput("range.in <http://range.in>", "Selecte a value in the range of data", min=min(mydata), value=mean(mydata), max=max(mydata), step=diff(range(mydata))/10)
  })

  output$range.out <- renderPrint({
    (input$range.in <http://range.in>)^2
  })

})

Suggestion:

  A) add an optional field or fields class= and style= to all input functions which decorate the inputs with classes and styles specified
  B) provide wrapper functions for applying classes and styles.

-Alex

runMyApp <- function() {

messages.subject: Re: file.choose() problem on glimmer.rstudio.com
messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

The file.choose() function launches an Open dialog box right out of the R process. In this case, the R process is running on our server and is not interactive (interactive() == FALSE), so R knows that file.choose() can never succeed.

Where are the files you want to rename? Are they on the server, or on your Mac? If on the server, one (ugly) workaround would be to have a textbox where you can paste in the full path of the folder.

messages.body_plain:
There is not, but calling "window.location.reload()" in JavaScript might achieve that effect (though it will also start a new session). So you could do something like this:

In ui.R:
uiOutput("reload")

In server.R:
output$reload <- renderUI({
  if (input$saveButton > 0) {
    tags$script("window.location.reload();")
  }
})

So that JS would be pushed to the client only after saveButton was pressed.

messages.subject: New features in development version of Shiny
messages.subject_clean: New features in development version of Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We've recently added some new features to the development version of Shiny. If you're feeling adventurous (or if you like finding bugs), you can install the latest version with:
  install.packages('httpuv')
  install.packages('devtools')  # Install devtools if needed
  devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

The new features include:

* A new reactive values object named clientData, which carries information about the client browser and can be accessed inside the shinyServer function. The information includes the hidden status of output objects, height/width plot output objects, and the URL of the browser.

* A new function `renderImage()`, which lets you send any image files to the client, not just ones generated by R's normal graphical device system.

* Support for high-resolution (Retina) displays. Plots generated by renderPlot() will automatically be created at higher resolution if the client is using a high-res display.

* Support for the new httpuv package, which makes file uploading work properly with Shiny server.

* A new method for detecting hidden output objects. Instead of checking that height and width are 0, it checks that the object or any ancestor in the DOM  has style display:none.

We also have some pages in the tutorial that explain how to use these new features. Until the new version is officially released, these pages will only be in tutorial page from my repository here:
  http://wch.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#client-data
  http://wch.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#sending-images

Enjoy!
-Winston

Op vrijdag 4 januari 2013 22:28:20 UTC+1 schreef Joe Cheng [RStudio] het volgende:

> A number of you have tried to use the actionButton that's included in shiny-incubator to perform actions, and sometimes those actions needed to read from other reactive inputs. Until now, changes to those other inputs would cause the action to be re-executed, with no clean way to suppress those extra executions.
>
> We just checked in a change to the GitHub repository that should improve things quite a bit. I'm not sure this will be our final solution to this problem, but welcome your feedback.
>
> The change is a new function called "isolate", and it lets you execute code that reads from reactive values/functions, without having their reactivity "infect" the caller.
>
> So a reactive data frame that only recalculates itself when an action button (with the id "recalcButton") is pressed might look like this:
>
> mydata <- reactive(function() {
>   # Don't do anything until after the first button push.
>   if (input$recalcButton == 0)
>     return(NULL)
>
>   # Note that just by virtue of checking the value of input$recalcButton,
>   # we're now going to get called whenever it is pushed.
>
>   return(isolate({
>     # Now do the expensive stuff
>     foo <- activateInterlock(input$foo)
>     bar <- connectDynotherm(input$bar)

messages.subject: Shiny ReactiveUI
messages.body_plain:
The addition of this function is fantastic.  It allows for a much greater flexibility in my webapps; however, if I could make a suggestion to the Shiny developers:

Adding a new function to pass commands directly to the browser console will make the interface drastically more flexible, and allow for full implementation of d3 commands within R.  All that is necessary is a command, such as:

ConsoleCommand('var header = d3.select("#chart").append("svg:svg")
.attr("width", window.innerWidth)
.attr("height", 50)
.append("text")
.attr("id", "header")
.attr("dy", 25)
.attr("dx", "50%")
.text(headerText);')

This would only require the addition of the following to the Shiny JavaScript:

function onMessage(msg) {
eval(msg.data);
}

I can do some of these commands by including the string as a command in the ReactiveUI function; however, this method would be faster and would not require modifying the HTML file for every command.  Unfortunately, I am not able to implement this change myself by adding a js file to the app folder because I have no way to access the value of the websocket in order to use websocket_write(command, WS).  As an aside, accessing this value would be beneficial for apps that require significant calculation time in R, e.g. Markov chain Monte Carlo methods where I would prefer to update the app during a function that may take a few hours to complete.  Like I said, the ReactiveUI function is a great addition and has a lot of potential for fully integrating R into the web.

-Chris

messages.subject: Re: Nested uiOutput error: input => uiOutput => uiOutput => output
messages.subject_clean: Nested uiOutput error: input => uiOutput => uiOutput => output
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, this was a bug in Shiny. If a uiOutput displayed a control (i.e. the slider), and then later displayed an error, then any future instances of the previously displayed control would stop working.

I've fixed this on GitHub, in the meantime you can work around it by having output$range check its inputs carefull and if proceeding will result in an error, just return NULL. Or use tryCatch.

On Sun, Mar 17, 2013 at 10:25 AM, Johnson Hsieh <eul...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi all,
> I have a problem for design a nested input/output app.
> My app can be simplified as the following steps:
> 0. Input dataset by textarea. i.e.: input$textarea.in <http://textarea.in>
> 1. Load dataset and show the name list of the imported dataset. User could select data by selectInput.  i.e: uiOutput("choosedata")
> 2. Compute the range of selected data and then display a sliderInput. i.e.: uiOutput("range")
> 3. Finally, compute the square of value selected by sliderInput. i.e.:verbatimTextOutput("range.out")
>
> That is:
> input$textare.in <http://textare.in> => output$choosedata => input$dataset => output$range => input$range.in <http://range.in> => output$range.out
>                    |________uiOutput/renderUI________|     |_____uiOutput/renderUI_____|      (error here!)
>
>
> The error will happen at step 3 after changing imported dataset.
> To be more specific, the initial input format is:
> Data.A 1 2 3 4 5
> Data.B 6 7 8 9 10 11
>

messages.subject: Re: Shiny ReactiveUI
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I'm a little leery of making this a supported idiom, as it cuts against the grain of the Shiny model to want something done "right now"--it's more imperative while the Shiny model is more declarative.

That said, I would love to let you do some hacking on this albeit in a not-officially-supported way. I believe you can write directly to the websocket from within server.R like this:

.subset2(input, "impl")$.websocket$send(foo)

where foo is either a raw vector or UTF-8 encoded string.

You'll want to use the GitHub version of Shiny [devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")] as it moves away from the "websockets" package and depends on our new "httpuv" package instead.

It looks to me like you've discovered the oncustommessage hook in shiny.js, which you can override by setting Shiny.oncustommessage; that's really the only other piece you need. I will find it slightly surprising though if you don't run into challenges trying to get these messages sent to the client at exactly the right time.

Good luck!

messages.subject: Re: Shiny ReactiveUI
messages.body_plain:
While working a different issue, I actually implemented something that allows sending arbitrary Javascript from the server to the client -- but I ended up not keeping this code for that issue. However, I've cleaned it up and put it in this branch:
  https://github.com/wch/shiny/tree/eval-js

You can install with:
  devtools::install_github('shiny', 'wch', 'eval-js')
You will also need to have httpuv.

I've modified the 01_hello example to demonstrate how to use it:
  https://gist.github.com/wch/5202490

On the server end, you add an evalJsHandler like this:
  output$test_eval <- evalJsHandler({
    paste("alert('Hello World! obs is ", input$obs, ".');", sep = "")
  })

Somewhere in ui.r, you add a jsEvaluator:
    jsEvaluator("test_eval")

I don't know if this will actually be useful for your particular case, since the server doesn't necessarily send the Javascript immediately to the client. It will send the Javascript code along with everything else, when all the reactive outputs have finished executing and their output is flushed (I think).

Please keep in mind that this is at best something to experiment with. If we were to add something like this for real, we'd need to consider more carefully the design and implementation.

-Winston

> > > A number of you have tried to use the actionButton that's included in shiny-incubator to perform actions, and sometimes those actions needed to read from other reactive inputs. Until now, changes to those other inputs would cause the action to be re-executed, with no clean way to suppress those extra executions.
> > >
> > > We just checked in a change to the GitHub repository that should improve things quite a bit. I'm not sure this will be our final solution to this problem, but welcome your feedback.
> > >
> > > The change is a new function called "isolate", and it lets you execute code that reads from reactive values/functions, without having their reactivity "infect" the caller.
> > >
> > > So a reactive data frame that only recalculates itself when an action button (with the id "recalcButton") is pressed might look like this:
> > >
> > > mydata <- reactive(function() {
> > >   # Don't do anything until after the first button push.
> > >   if (input$recalcButton == 0)
> > >     return(NULL)
> > >
> > >   # Note that just by virtue of checking the value of input$recalcButton,
> > >   # we're now going to get called whenever it is pushed.
> > >
> > >   return(isolate({
> > >     # Now do the expensive stuff
> > >     foo <- activateInterlock(input$foo)
> > >     bar <- connectDynotherm(input$bar)
> > >     baz <- bringInfracellsUp(input$baz)
> > >     c(foo=foo, bar=bar, baz=baz)
> > >   }))
> > > })
> > >
> > > So mydata will automatically react to changes in recalcButton (i.e. when it is pushed) but not to changes in the inputs foo, bar, or baz.
> > >
> > > How to install
> > >
> > > If you'd like to try isolate out for yourself, you can conveniently install the latest build from github using these commands:
> > >
> > > install.package("devtools")  # if necessary
> > > devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")
> > >
> > > (Glimmer users: We generally keep Glimmer synced to the version of Shiny that's on CRAN, so isolate probably won't be available there for at least a couple of weeks. Sorry.)

messages.subject: Re: Showing POSIXt object with Shiny renderTable

messages.body_plain:
renderTable uses xtable() to generate the output, and it looks like xtable doesn't play well with dates in general:

library(xtable)
dat <- data.frame(date=as.POSIXlt(Sys.time()), x=1:5)
print(xtable(dat))
# Error in Math.POSIXt(x + ifelse(x == 0, 1, 0)) :
#   'abs' not defined for "POSIXt" objects

I've filed an issue here:
  https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/129

In the meantime, a workaround is to convert the relevant columns to characters:
  http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8652674/r-xtable-and-dates

-Winston

On Monday, 18 March 2013 11:24:29 UTC-7, Winston Chang wrote:
> Hi everyone -
>
> We've recently added some new features to the development version of Shiny. If you're feeling adventurous (or if you like finding bugs), you can install the latest version with:
>   install.packages('httpuv')
>   install.packages('devtools')  # Install devtools if needed
>   devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')
>
>
> The new features include:
>
> * A new reactive values object named clientData, which carries information about the client browser and can be accessed inside the shinyServer function. The information includes the hidden status of output objects, height/width plot output objects, and the URL of the browser.
>
> * A new function `renderImage()`, which lets you send any image files to the client, not just ones generated by R's normal graphical device system.
>
> * Support for high-resolution (Retina) displays. Plots generated by renderPlot() will automatically be created at higher resolution if the client is using a high-res display.
>
> * Support for the new httpuv package, which makes file uploading work properly with Shiny server.
>
> * A new method for detecting hidden output objects. Instead of checking that height and width are 0, it checks that the object or any ancestor in the DOM  has style display:none.
>
> We also have some pages in the tutorial that explain how to use these new features. Until the new version is officially released, these pages will only be in tutorial page from my repository here:
>   http://wch.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#client-data
>   http://wch.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#sending-images
>
>
> Enjoy!
> -Winston

Hi Andrew -

I've updated the page to include the corresponding ui.r example code. I've also put the code at:
  https://gist.github.com/wch/5214648
so you can use
  runGist(5214648)

One slight change: although they are interchangeable now, it's more appropriate to use imageOutput() instead of plotOutput(). They have the same effect now, but in the future it's conceivable that they could diverge.

If you still have problems, I'd suggest re-installing shiny from Github and restarting R. And if you still have problems with it, please let us know...

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: shiny server and how to know the process.
messages.subject_clean: shiny server and how to know the process.
messages.body_plain:
There is no general solution to this problem (predict how long the server will be busy) but it would be possible to add calls within your own code to calculate how many units of data you have processed, how many are left, how much time has elapsed, estimate how much time is remaining, etc. However, Shiny currently does not have a way to send custom progress messages while it is busy executing; instead it will mark each output component as "in progress" and then unmark them all simultaneously when execution completes. We hope to add a way to do custom progress in the future though.

messages.subject: error in using conditionalPanel(sliderInput(...)) - shiny 0.2 vs shiny 0.4.0
messages.subject_clean: error in using conditionalPanel(sliderInput(...)) - shiny 0.2 vs shiny 0.4.0
messages.body_plain:
All,

I recently updated to shiny 0.4.0 and have run into a new error running an app built (and working normally) under shiny 0.2. The app runs normally except when I try to use the conditionalPanel(sliderInput(...)). If I do try to use it, I get an error but the app does not crash. Have there been any changes to the use of these tools between versions? Any help would be appreciated.

Any help would be greatly appreciated

Here is the console log:
> runApp(launch=T)

Listening on port 8100
Error in if (del == 0 && to == 0) return(to) :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
Error in if (del == 0 && to == 0) return(to) :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

The ui.R script includes the following:
#------------------------------------
## ui.R
#------------------------------------
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 # sidebar with controls to allow user to define graphical elements and how
  # they want them displayed.
  sidebarPanel(

# (... omitted- a wellPanel() allowing users to select which plots to display)

# allow the user to subset their demographics by age range
    checkboxInput(inputId= "subset_age", label= "Would you like to 'zoom-in' on a specific age range?",
                  value= FALSE),

    conditionalPanel(condition= "input.subset_age",
                     sliderInput("age_sub", "Please select the age range you would like to 'zoom-in' on:",
                                 min= 18, max= 85, value= c(18,85))
    )
),
# mainPanel() - for conditionalPanel(plotOutput(...))
)

The server.R script includes the following:
#------------------------------------
# Server.R
#------------------------------------
# (omitted) - data loading, plot rendering, etc

demoUpdate <- reactive(function() {
    # subset demos on age, based on user input

    if (input$subset_age == TRUE) {
      demos2 <- demos[demos$age > input$age_sub[1] & demos$age < input$age_sub[2],]
      return(demos2)
    } else {
      demos <- demos[complete.cases(demos[, c(4:11, 13:14)]) , c(2, 4:14)]
      return(demos)
    }
  })

messages.subject: Re: Setting outputOptions with "suspendWhenHidden=FALSE" triggers an error message
messages.subject_clean: Setting outputOptions with "suspendWhenHidden=FALSE" triggers an error message
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for sharing the code! It helped us find a small bug, and we also learned from it that we need to document a part about objects being shown/hidden.

The bug was that renderPlot() didn't properly handle empty values for height and width. That's been fixed and pushed to the development branch.

The second issue is that with the recent shown/hidden changes, you need to explicitly trigger a 'shown' event when objects become visible, and a 'hidden' event when they become invisible. This event (I believe) isn't a standard Javascript event that automatically gets triggered when objects become visible, so your Javascript code needs to do it. If you modify your xwizard.js file and add the following lines, it should work:

function disablePanel(panelid) {
    $("#step" + panelid).removeClass("active");
    $("#lbl-step" + panelid).removeClass("active");
    $("#lbl-step" + panelid).trigger("hidden"); // Add this line
}

function navigateToPanel(panelid) {
    $("#step" + panelid).addClass("active");
    $("#lbl-step" + panelid).addClass("active");
    $("#lbl-step" + panelid).trigger("shown"); // Add this line
}

Even with this change to the Javascript, you may momentarily see an error message when it switches to the second tab, before it is replaced by the plots. The error is related to the height/width bug I mentioned above. We're going to release a new version of Shiny to CRAN very soon, and once you update to that version, the error message should disappear.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Shiny - the future
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

On Friday, March 22, 2013, qubz wrote:
> I have a few questions:
>
> 1. What is the future for Shiny, will it be developed beyond the end of the year?

We certainly intend to work on it for the foreseeable future. We consider it to be a strategically important product for our company and are investing in it accordingly.

> 2. How big is the user base and how many sites/apps using Shiny are there?

It's almost impossible to say when the entire software stack is open source and distributed by CRAN mirrors around the world. That said, judging by the activity on this mailing list and by the number of stars/forks on our GitHub repo, we are very happy with the amount of interest around Shiny.

> 3. Does it run server-side or client-side?

The R code runs on the server side. You can do further processing in JavaScript on the client side for more advanced scenarios.

On Tuesday, March 19, 2013 7:56:44 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Hi Chris,
>
> I'm a little leery of making this a supported idiom, as it cuts against the grain of the Shiny model to want something done "right now"--it's more imperative while the Shiny model is more declarative.
>
> That said, I would love to let you do some hacking on this albeit in a not-officially-supported way. I believe you can write directly to the websocket from within server.R like this:
>
> .subset2(input, "impl")$.websocket$send(foo)
>
> where foo is either a raw vector or UTF-8 encoded string.
>
> You'll want to use the GitHub version of Shiny [devtools::install_github("shiny", "rstudio")] as it moves away from the "websockets" package and depends on our new "httpuv" package instead.
>
> It looks to me like you've discovered the oncustommessage hook in shiny.js, which you can override by setting Shiny.oncustommessage; that's really the only other piece you need. I will find it slightly surprising though if you don't run into challenges trying to get these messages sent to the client at exactly the right time.
>
> Good luck!
>
>
> On Tue, Mar 19, 2013 at 10:18 AM, Chris Hammack <pacif...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > The addition of this function is fantastic.  It allows for a much greater flexibility in my webapps; however, if I could make a suggestion to the Shiny developers:
> >
> > Adding a new function to pass commands directly to the browser console will make the interface drastically more flexible, and allow for full implementation of d3 commands within R.  All that is necessary is a command, such as:

> > .attr("width", window.innerWidth)
> > .attr("height", 50)
> > .append("text")
> > .attr("id", "header")
> > .attr("dy", 25)
> > .attr("dx", "50%")
> > .text(headerText);')
> >
> > This would only require the addition of the following to the Shiny JavaScript:
> >
> > function onMessage(msg) {
> > eval(msg.data);
> > }
> >
> > I can do some of these commands by including the string as a command in the ReactiveUI function; however, this method would be faster and would not require modifying the HTML file for every command.  Unfortunately, I am not able to implement this change myself by adding a js file to the app folder because I have no way to access the value of the websocket in order to use websocket_write(command, WS).  As an aside, accessing this value would be beneficial for apps that require significant calculation time in R, e.g. Markov chain Monte Carlo methods where I would prefer to update the app during a function that may take a few hours to complete.  Like I said, the ReactiveUI function is a great addition and has a lot of potential for fully integrating R into the web.

input_names <- c('A1', 'B1', 'C1')

for (in_name in input_names) {
  out_name <- paste('foo', in_name, sep = '')

  output[[out_name]] <- renderText({ ... input[[in_name]] ... })
}

messages.subject: Re: How to DRY many outputs?
messages.body_plain:
You also need to add another variable scope (local()) so that in_name is not shared between all the different renderText calls (this is an R thing, not a Shiny thing):

input_names <- c('A1', 'B1', 'C1')

for (in_name in input_names) {

  local({
    my_in_name <- in_name
    out_name <- paste('foo', my_in_name, sep = '')

    output[[out_name]] <<- renderText({ ... input[[my_in_name]] ... })
  })
}
