messages.subject: Re: How to DRY many outputs?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Winston, Joe.

On Monday, March 25, 2013 5:55:27 PM UTC+1, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> You also need to add another variable scope (local()) so that in_name is not shared between all the different renderText calls (this is an R thing, not a Shiny thing):
>

Thanks for the great suggestion: double-bracket indexing and local do the job.

The final code:

    output_names <- c(
        "profileA1",
        "profileB1",
        "profileA2",
        "profileB2",
        "profileA3",
        "profileB3",
        "profileA4",
        "profileB4"
    )
    reactive_names <- c(
        "game1PlayerAProfile",
        "game1PlayerBProfile",
        "game2PlayerAProfile",
        "game2PlayerBProfile",
        "game3PlayerAProfile",
        "game3PlayerBProfile",
        "game4PlayerAProfile",
        "game4PlayerBProfile"
    )

    for (out_name in output_names) {
        local({
            my_out_name <- out_name
            info_names <- c("Card", "Player", "Rating")
            for (info_name in info_names) {
                local({
                    my_info_name <- info_name
                    complete_out_name <- paste(my_out_name, my_info_name, sep = "")

                    output[[complete_out_name]] <<- renderText({
                        my_profile <- get(reactive_names[which(output_names == my_out_name)])()
                        my_profile[[tolower(my_info_name)]]
                    })
                })
            }
        })
    }

Regards,
Alberto

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the kind words!

In your example, input$cities is a character vector of the selected values. You could have put input$cities directly in the renderText at the end rather than wrapping it in citiesx; although citiesx would have worked as well IF in the renderText part you did "citiesx()" instead of "citiesx". (To read a reactive expression, you call it like a function.)

Next time you want to see what different variables look like, just put a browser() call in the middle of i.e. the renderText call there, and call runApp(). From the browse prompt you can just enter input$cities or whatever.

In the future we hope to make this particular scenario (using input A to populate input B) easier to accomplish without using reactiveUI at all.

-joe

Two issues here. 1) The both need id attributes, not name. (Or it's OK to have name, but you must also have id.) 2) If that alone doesn't fix it, try adding this after you set the selected index: $("#fixed_float").change(); Please let me know if that works for you; if so, and you need further explanation about why that fixes it, I would be happy to explain. Taking a step back, though, if you're presenting two mutually-exclusive sets of inputs or outputs, you might be better served with using tabsetPanel (note that if you give tabsetPanel an inputId, then your R code can know which tab is active); and if you prefer not to use tabsetPanel, then at least checkboxGroupInput for the Fixed/Float choice and use conditionalPanel to hide/show the relevant controls. messages.subject: request: synchronous input send squish
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,

   if it doesn't already, shiny should squish (merge) input messages until the latest output response - ie if an input change causes an long latency response, the next input message should be the merge of all pending input messages, rather than sending the queued input messages that would be sent while waiting for a response.

  Otherwise a long latency response will be followed by (potentially) N long latency responses.

-Alex

messages.subject: Re: sliderInput date range
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

first let me say: Your work is awesome. Shiny is a great tool.
According to solve the date slider I've tried to do it with an selectInput().
My basic data is an xts-Time Series.
When I'm trying to display just one hour of the time series there's no reaction of the plot, only the normal graph is plotted.
Maybe someone could help me to solve my problem. My UI and Server files are attached.

Thanks.
Daniel

UI.R

day<-sort(substr(index(apply.daily(DD.001,first)), 1, 10))
hour<-substr(index(hourly(DD.001[tag[2]], first)), 12, 16)

#UI definieren für Shiny

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

    headerPanel("Darstellung Messobjekte"),             #Anzeigetitel der Applikation

    sidebarPanel(
        selectInput(inputId="type",                         #Input ID
                    label="Zählertyp auswaehlen:",
                    list("Ultraschall"="Durchfluss1 KW",
                         "Ringkolben"="Durchfluss1 WW"
                              )),

        selectInput(inputId="date",                         #Input ID
                    label="Datum:",
                    day,
                    selected=4),

        selectInput(inputId="hour1",                         #Input ID
                    label="Stunde Beginn:",
                    hour),

        selectInput(inputId="hour2",                         #Input ID
                    label="Stunde Ende:",
                    hour,
                    selected=2)

        ),

    mainPanel(
        h3(textOutput("caption")),

        plotOutput("typePlot.daily"),

        plotOutput("typePlot.hourly"))

    ))

Server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

    formulaText <- reactive({
        paste(input$date, input$type)
        })

    output$caption <- renderText({
        formulaText()
    })

    output$typePlot.daily<-renderPlot({
        plot(DD.001[input$date,input$type],
             type="l",
             xlab="Datum",
             ylab="Durchfluss in L/s",
             main=NULL)
        })

    output$typePlot.hourly<-renderPlot({
        plot(x=index(DD.001[paste(paste(input$date, input$hour1, sep=""), paste(input$date, input$hour2, sep=""), sep="/")]),
            y=coredata(DD.001[(paste(paste(input$date, input$hour1, sep=""), paste(input$date, input$hour2, sep=""), sep="/")), input$type]),
             type="l",
             xlab="Datum",
             ylab="Durchfluss in L/s",
             main=NULL)
    })
})

I am developing an app with shiny googleVis. I have very big amount of data, it takes time before it does calculations so there's couple of problems I ran into.

So the question follows, is there any possibility to remove all outputs immediately if, for example, the slider value changes? Maybe it's possible to insert some kind of progress bar or processing bar..

Thank you in advance

messages.subject: Re: Variable number of inputs
messages.body_plain:
That actually isn't quite what I had in mind.  I am able to manipulate a single variable field at this point, my question is being able to create multiple fields and use their distinct inputs.

Suppose in one dataset, there are 3 columns to the annotation, HPV status (positive, negative), Cancer status (Tumor, Normal), and Stage (0,1,2,3,4), and the other dataset has 2 columns to the annotation, Subsite (lung, breast, colon, etc), Recurrence (positive, negative).  Selecting the first data set would create 3 input fields

HPV status
o positive
o negative

Cancer status
o Tumor
o Normal

Stage
o 0
o 1
o 2
o 3
o 4

while the other would produce:

Subsite
o lung
o breast
o colon
o other

Recurrence
o positive
o negative

Currently, I am capable of producing a single input field filled with the union of all of the potential selections (ie positive, negative, tumor, normal, 1, 2, 3, 4).  However, this is potentially troublesome when looking at how the data sets will be selected. If there is only one input field, either the union or intersection of the selected fields would be possible, however it is easy to imagine a situation where someone wanted to select one group of Tumors (all HPV status, all Stages) and one group of Normals (all HPV status, all Stages)- taking the union of all matches would yield every sample in each of the two groups (all samples are either HPV positive or negative), while taking the intersect would result in the two groups being empty (no sample can be both HPV positive and HPV negative).  As such, I need a way to organize it to be the union of the selected within columns, and intersect between them, to subset the data.  Does this clarify what I am after?

Thanks!
Mike

messages.body_plain:
I send you my two functions for this task:

The first function is for getting one ui element and the second one puts them together. The iProfile variable is used for comparing the same dataset on different selection, e.g. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

#' Create a ui element for the profile
#'
#' This function builds an ui element, e.g. slider, numerics for the profile
#'
#' @param object The CancerStorage class
#' @param iPObjekt The integer number of the object to build
#' @param iProfil The profile ID
#'
#' @return a ui element
#'
#' @export
getProfileObject <- function(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=1) {

  if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "slider") {

    # sliderInput
    rn <- range(object@dtData[[object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt]]])
    sliderInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""),
                label   = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt],
                min     = rn[1],
                max     = rn[2],
                value   = c(rn[1], rn[2]),
                step    = 1,
                format  = "####")

  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "select") {

    # selectInput
    selectInput(inputId = paste(object@lProfile@cInputID[iPObjekt], "P", iProfil, sep=""),
          label         = object@lProfile@cLabel[iPObjekt],
          choices       = object@lProfile@lChoices[[iPObjekt]] )

  } else if (object@lProfile@cShinyClass[iPObjekt] == "numeric") {

    # numericInput

  } else {

  }

}

#' Create the profile UI
#'
#' This function builds the ui wih the sliders, inputs etc. profile for the
#' user interaction
#'
#' @param object The CancerStorage -Class
#' @param ... Tnput variables
#'
#' @return A sidebar ui panel of the profile
#'
#' @export
buildProfileUI <- function(object, iProfile=1) {

  m <- length(object@lProfile@cInputID)
  lP <- list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=1, iProfil=iProfile), br())
  for (i in 2:(m-1)) {
    lP <- c(lP,
            list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=i, iProfil=iProfile)),
            list(br()))
  }
  lP <- c(lP, list(getProfileObject(object, iPObjekt=m, iProfil=iProfile)))
  lP

}

messages.subject: Re: transition of outputs or results
messages.body_plain:
By default we attempt to change the opacity on any outputs that are recalculating (see example <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/diamonds/>). If that's not what you want (or in this case, apparently not working on gvisTable), you can use the CSS class "recalculating" that is immediately added to any outputs that we know are going to be recomputed. You could add this to your ui.R (for example in the sidebarPanel or mainPanel) to hide recalculating outputs:

tags$style(type="text/css", ".recalculating {visibility: hidden}")

On Fri, Mar 29, 2013 at 6:54 AM, <couch...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I am developing an app with shiny googleVis. I have very big amount of data, it takes time before it does calculations so there's couple of problems I ran into.
>
> Suppose this app <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/mages/Example_2/> to be an example. You can see that it has a data printed out in the table. If you click on radio button the calculation appears and table becomes pageable.  However, you can notice that some time, after you pressed the radio button, the table remains unchanged. If you have lots of calculations this time becomes longer and sometimes it's hard to know whether your data already updated or no.
>
> So the question follows, is there any possibility to remove all outputs immediately if, for example, the slider value changes? Maybe it's possible to insert some kind of progress bar or processing bar..
>
> Thank you in advance

You almost have it.

checkboxGroupInput returns the HTML for that control. (The same is true for any of the other input/output functions you use in ui.R.) In your "for" loop, you're creating the HTML and then dropping it on the floor. You just need to collect them in a list and return it, then it should work.

output$subsetControl <- renderUI({
  lapply(1:ncol(datasetInput()), function(i) {

    subss <-    unique(datasetInput()[,i])
    checkboxGroupInput(paste("subsst",i,sep=""), colnames(datasetInput())[i], choices=subss, selected=subss)
  })

})

messages.subject: Re: Tabsets and linked update
messages.body_plain:
I think there is still some problems with using tabset with actionbutton. For example, if you are currently one a tab that doesn't do computationally-intensive task, you will see the update right away. So far so good. But if there is a computationally-intensive task on the tab (in my case, it's graph), the content in that tab remains the same, even though it's doing some intensive computation and will return something to the user after a while. However, from the user's perspective, she won't know if the app is working hard to render the result. So this is not user-friendly. I would suggest give some kind of feedbacks to the user when the user switches to the computationally-intensive tab (like shading it), so that the user knows she should wait for the result.
